method: Hand computation from this vector's input.json and conventions.json together with docs/CONVENTIONS.md and the METRIC_DEFINITIONS in src/types.ts. No metric-computing code was written, imported or run, and no expected.json was opened while this file was produced.
rounding: Half-up to four decimal places; terminating values left exact.

warnings.detail: Row w06 carries the sex value X, which this vector's declared sexMapping of {F:F, M:M} does not cover. The row is counted in excludedN on every metric and is never silently dropped.

resolutions.whatWasAmbiguous: What metric (e)'s single scalar denotes, given that Art. 9(1)(e) names two figures and MetricValue carries one.
resolutions.secondPassOriginallyChose: The overall proportion of workers receiving a component — 100 here.
resolutions.firstPassChose: The difference between the two per-sex proportions, in percentage points — 0 here.
resolutions.nowReads: CONVENTIONS.md, componentMap: the scalar is the MALE proportion minus the FEMALE proportion, in percentage points, positive meaning men are the more likely to receive components.
resolutions.why: Every other metric position in this report is a female-versus-male comparison expressed against the male figure; a bare overall proportion would be the only figure in the report that is not one. The settled reading also disposes of a question the proportion reading could not answer here — whether the unmapped w06, who does receive a component, belongs in the numerator: under a per-sex difference the question does not arise, because w06 is in neither group.

resolutions.whatWasAmbiguous: Which of the four quartile bands metric (f)'s single scalar reports, given that Art. 9(1)(f) names eight figures.
resolutions.secondPassOriginallyChose: The lowest band's female share — 100 here.
resolutions.firstPassChose: The highest band's female share — 0 here.
resolutions.nowReads: CONVENTIONS.md, quartileTieRule: the female share of the HIGHEST (fourth) quartile pay band, as a percentage.
resolutions.why: Attributable to the same national guidance document this key already borrows its tie rule from. Both passes had already built IDENTICAL bands from the SAME six-worker ranking; only the band reported differed.

resolutions.whatWasAmbiguous: Whether a row whose sex value the map does not cover still takes part in the quartile RANKING, and what populationN counts once the ranked and sexed populations differ.
resolutions.secondPassOriginallyChose: Ranked but not counted; populationN 5, excludedN 1.
resolutions.firstPassChose: The same on both points — the two passes AGREED and no number changed. The first pass recorded the reason in its W_SEX_UNMAPPED detail: a quartile pay band is a division of the whole workforce by pay level.
resolutions.nowReads: CONVENTIONS.md, sexMapping: an unmapped row keeps its place in the pay ranking because Art. 3(1)(f) divides workers by pay level and an unmapped worker is still a worker; it is excluded only from the female and male counts. populationN is the SEXED population, with the unmapped rows in excludedN. An unmapped value is not `other` or `undisclosed`.
resolutions.why: Recorded despite the agreement, because the exclusion rule settled the sex breakdown and said nothing about the ranking, and the two are different questions. Striking the row from the ranking would move other workers between bands with nothing in the report to show why.

working.step0_payDefinition: BASE basic, BONUS complementary_variable, nothing excluded. Every worker has the same BONUS of 300, which is deliberate: it makes metrics (b) and (d) exactly zero and so isolates the unmapped-sex question from any component arithmetic.
step1_perWorkerTotals: w06 X Sales 3500 + 300 = 3800  <-- sex value not covered by sexMapping
working.step2_sexSplit: sexMapping is {F:F, M:M}. w06's value X is not a key in it. The sexMapping convention states that such a row goes to excludedN with W_SEX_UNMAPPED and is never silently dropped. So the sexed population is two women (w01, w02) and three men (w03, w04, w05): populationN 5, excludedN 1 on every metric. Note that the mapping does NOT route X to the SexCode other or undisclosed — those codes exist for values an employer's map assigns to them, and this map assigns nothing to X at all.
working.step3_metricA: Female totals 3000+3400 = 6400 over two, mean 3200. Male totals 3600+4000+4400 = 12000 over three, mean 4000. (4000-3200)/4000 = 800/4000 = 0.20 -> 20. w06's 3800 enters neither mean. Had it been silently folded into one of them, the gap would have moved and nothing in the report would have shown why — which is the failure this vector exists to catch.
working.step4_metricB: Female BONUS 300 and 300, mean 300. Male BONUS 300, 300, 300, mean 300. (300-300)/300 = 0/300 = 0 -> 0. This zero is NOT W_COMPONENTS_ALL_ZERO: both figures are 300, not zero, and the denominator is well defined. It is an ordinary zero difference.
working.step5_metricC: Female headcount is EVEN at two, so lower_of_two applies: ascending 3000, 3400 -> both are middle values -> 3000. Male headcount is odd at three -> middle 4000. (4000-3000)/4000 = 1000/4000 = 0.25 -> 25. The median gap is wider than the mean gap because lower_of_two takes the lower of the two women.
working.step6_metricD: Female BONUS ascending 300, 300 -> lower_of_two takes 300, the two candidates being equal. Male BONUS median 300. (300-300)/300 = 0 -> 0.
working.step7_metricE: All five sexed workers have a BONUS of 300, strictly positive: 2 of 2 women and 3 of 3 men receive a component. Under the settled rule the scalar is 100 - 100 = 0 percentage points, over populationN 5 with excludedN 1. (Originally reported as the overall proportion, 100; see resolutions.) w06 also receives a component, but it cannot be attributed to a sex, and under a per-sex difference the question of which side to count it on does not arise at all.

step8_quartiles.rankingPopulation: Six workers are RANKED, including w06. Only five are COUNTED in the female and male shares. See the ambiguity below — this is the fork this vector exposes.
step8_quartiles.sizes: n = 6 ranked gives 6 = 4 x 1 + 2. Under to_lower: sizes 2, 2, 1, 1. Boundaries after positions 2, 4 and 5.
step8_quartiles.tie: No two workers share a total pay level; quartileTieRule is not exercised.

composition.Q1: w01 F, w02 F -> 2 women, 0 men -> 100 percent female
composition.Q2: w03 M, w06 X -> 0 women, 1 man, 1 unmapped -> 0 percent female

step8_quartiles.scalarChosen: 0, the female share of the HIGHEST quartile pay band, per the settled rule. (Originally the lowest band, 100; see resolutions.)
step8_quartiles.counterfactual: Had w06 been struck from the ranking as well, n would be 5 with sizes 2, 1, 1, 1, and Q2 would hold w03 alone while Q3 held w04 and Q4 held w05. Under the settled rule the reported scalar is the Q4 female share, which is 0 either way, so the fork changes nothing visible here — as it also changed nothing under the lowest-band reading, where both give 100. The fork does change the band membership of three of the five sexed workers, and any future vector with a differently placed unmapped row would expose it. That this vector cannot distinguish the two readings at ALL is itself worth recording: the ranking question is settled in the convention document rather than by evidence from these rows.

working.step9_metricG: One category, Sales, holding all six rows, five of them sexed. The category gap equals metric (a) at 20, over populationN 5 with excludedN 1.
working.step10_suppression: minGroupSize null: no suppression, no unreliability. The female group of two is small but no threshold is set.
working.step11_art10: Sales at 20 clears the five-point trigger and is flagged.

ambiguities.issue: Whether a row whose sex value the map does not cover still takes part in the QUARTILE RANKING, or is struck from the population entirely. The convention says it goes to excludedN and is never silently dropped, which settles the sex breakdown but not the ranking.
readings: Ranked but not counted — the worker is still a worker whose pay level sits in the distribution, so the quartile boundaries reflect the real workforce and only the female and male shares omit them.
Struck entirely — the worker is outside every metric, so the quartiles are built from the five sexed workers alone.
ambiguities.why: Art. 3(1)(f) divides WORKERS into four equal groups by pay level, and w06 is a worker. Removing them from the ranking moves other workers between bands without any trace in the report, which is the same silent-distortion failure the sexMapping convention was written to prevent one metric along. But the wording genuinely does not decide it, and the choice changes band membership.

ambiguities.issue: Whether populationN for metric (f) counts the ranked population or the sexed population, given the two now differ.
readings: 5, the number of workers whose sex the metric could report.
ambiguities.why: MetricValue documents populationN as the workers counted IN THIS FIGURE, and the figure is a female share, which w06 cannot enter. Reporting 6 would imply the share has a denominator of six. The consequence is that populationN + excludedN happens to equal the ranked headcount here, which is tidy but coincidental.

ambiguities.issue: Scope of metrics (a) and (c): total pay, or ordinary basic wage or salary alone.
readings: Basic only, per the payBasis heading's SEPARATELY wording.
ambiguities.why: Under the other reading metric (a) runs over BASE alone: female mean 2900, male mean 3700, giving 21.6216 rather than 20.

ambiguities.issue: Metric (e) is a two-sided proportion carried in a one-scalar MetricValue.
readings: The overall proportion receiving a component.
The percentage-point difference between the two proportions.
ambiguities.chosen: The overall proportion receiving a component
ambiguities.why: The difference reading reads zero everywhere and erases v09's intended contrast. Here it raises a second question the difference reading cannot answer either: whether w06, who does receive a component, belongs in the numerator.
ambiguities.supersededBy: resolutions[0] — the difference reading now governs, and it in fact ANSWERS the w06 question this entry raised against it: under a per-sex difference w06 is in neither group and never enters the numerator. The coverage objection is carried forward under componentMap in CONVENTIONS.md.

ambiguities.issue: Metric (f) is eight numbers carried in a one-scalar MetricValue.
ambiguities.chosen: The female share of the lowest quartile pay band
ambiguities.supersededBy: resolutions[1] — the HIGHEST band now governs.
